title: Quadratic universal simulation
statement: Let $c$ be an effective machine-coding scheme. There is a finite-tape machine $U$ over the Boolean alphabet such that, for every finite-tape Boolean machine $M_0$, function $f$ on finite Boolean strings, and time bound $T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, if $M_0$ computes $f(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every input $x$, then there are a Boolean string $\alpha$ and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every Boolean string $x$, $U$ computes $f(x)$ on the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ within $C\,(T(|x|)+1)^2$ steps.
hypotheses_covered: $M_0$ is a finite-tape machine over the Boolean alphabet
$f$ maps finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings
$M_0$ computes $f(x)$ within $T(|x|)$ steps for every input $x$
replaced:
For every effective machine-coding scheme, there is a single finite-tape machine $U$
over the binary alphabet such that the following holds. For every finite-tape binary
machine $M_0$, function $f$ on finite bit strings, and time bound
$T\colon\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, if $M_0$ computes $f$ on every input within time $T$
of the input length, then there are a bit string $\alpha$ and a constant
$C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every bit string $x$, $U$ computes $f(x)$ on the paired
encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ within $C\,(T(|x|)+1)^2$ steps.
